title: Death Sentence
full_review:
He did it for the wife (Kelly Preston) and kids, Brendan (Stuart Lafferty) and Lucas (Jordan Garrett). That�s the lame excuse for "Death Sentence" (Fox), in which mild-mannered financier Nick Hume (Kevin Bacon) commits capital murder on members of a gang after older son Brendan becomes the victim of one of their random killings.

For the first hour, director James Wan (best-known for "Saw") and screenwriter Ian Jeffers follow the nuances of novelist Brian Garfield�s 1975 sequel to "Death Wish" and sprinkle in touches of mordant humor. The last half-hour descends into splatter, heavy-handed symbolism, and an apparent homage to Martin Scorsese�s "Taxi Driver."

Performances by Garrett Hedlund as soulful gang leader Billy Darley, and big John Goodman as over-the-top gun dealer (and father of Billy) Bones Darley are quite compelling. Bacon, an appealing and believable actor, makes an implausible madman.

In movies of this type, the court system is always a sham, there�s never a police officer around when you need one, and Aisha Tyler as Detective Wallis is given such idiotic lines as asking Hume, "Why don�t you tell me what�s going on?"

The best of the action sequences has Hume chased through a parking garage by the gang, although he�s so acrobatic and energetic, one almost expects to hear "Footloose" on the soundtrack.
